title: Multiplayer Structural Load Stress Visualization
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements a multiplayer structural load stress visualization for architectural analysis. The scene simulates a building frame where multiple simulated 'players' can place loads on structural members and observe real-time stress propagation.

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark background (0x1a1a2e) with ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and two directional lights: one from top-right (0xffffff, intensity 0.8, position 10,15,10) and one fill light (0x8888ff, intensity 0.3, position -5,5,-5).
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera FOV 60, positioned at (20, 15, 20) looking at origin. Add OrbitControls.
- Build a 3-story steel frame structure centered at origin:
  - 4 columns (vertical beams) at corners: positions (±5, 0, ±5), each 12 units tall, using CylinderGeometry(0.2, 0.2, 4) stacked 3 segments per column.
  - 3 floor levels at y=4, y=8, y=12 with horizontal beams connecting columns (BoxGeometry for beams, 0.15 height, 0.2 depth).
  - Each beam and column segment is a separate mesh for individual stress coloring.
  - Ground plane: 30x30, color 0x2a2a3a, at y=0.
- Label each structural member with an ID (e.g., 'C1_S1' for column 1 segment 1, 'B1_F2' for beam 1 floor 2).

## Stress Simulation Physics
- Each structural member has properties: maxLoad (columns: 1000 kN, beams: 500 kN), currentLoad (starts 0), stressRatio (currentLoad/maxLoad).
- Stress propagation: when a load is placed on a floor beam, it distributes to connected members. Vertical loads transfer 50% to the beam directly, 25% to each adjacent column below. Loads accumulate downward — lower floors bear more.
- Stress color mapping: stressRatio 0.0 = green (0x00ff00), 0.0-0.5 = green to yellow gradient, 0.5-0.8 = yellow to orange, 0.8-1.0 = orange to red (0xff0000), >1.0 = flashing red (failure state).
- Total structural integrity = 100% minus weighted average of all stressRatios (clamped 0-100).

## Multiplayer Simulation
- Simulate 3 players: 'Player1' (color 0xff4444), 'Player2' (color 0x44ff44), 'Player3' (color 0x4444ff).
- Each player has a cursor sphere (radius 0.3) visible in the scene at their current target position.
- The real user controls Player1 via mouse raycasting on floor planes.
- Player2 and Player3 are AI-driven: every 3 seconds they randomly select a floor beam and place/remove a load.

## User Interactions
- Click on any floor beam to place a 100 kN load as Player1. Click again on a loaded beam to remove the load.
- Press '1','2','3' keys to toggle visibility of each player's loads (filter view).
- Press 'R' to reset all loads to zero.
- Press 'S' to toggle stress propagation mode: 'instant' (default) vs 'animated' (loads visually ripple through structure over 500ms).
- Press 'F' to toggle a 'failure analysis' overlay that highlights members above 80% stress with pulsing outlines.
- A DOM button 'Add Earthquake Load' applies a random 50-200 kN load to every beam simultaneously.
- A DOM button 'Export Report' logs the current stress state summary to console and updates a report div.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left panel: 'Structural Integrity: XX%', 'Total Load: XXXX kN', 'Members at Risk: X'.
- Top-right panel: Player list showing each player name, color dot, and number of loads placed.
- Bottom bar: current propagation mode ('Instant'/'Animated'), failure overlay status ('ON'/'OFF').
- Style all UI with semi-transparent dark backgrounds, white text, monospace font.

## State Management — window.__3D_STATE__
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- structuralIntegrity: number (0-100)
- totalLoad: number (sum of all loads in kN)
- membersAtRisk: number (count of members with stressRatio > 0.8)
- memberCount: number (total structural members)
- members: array of {id: string, type: 'column'|'beam', stressRatio: number, currentLoad: number, floor: number}
- players: array of {name: string, loadCount: number, visible: boolean}
- propagationMode: 'instant' | 'animated'
- failureOverlay: boolean
- failedMembers: number (count of members with stressRatio > 1.0)
- lastAction: string (description of last action taken, e.g., 'Player1 placed 100kN on B1_F2')
- earthquakeApplied: boolean
- playerLoads: object mapping player names to arrays of {memberId: string, amount: number}
- maxStressRatio: number (highest stressRatio among all members)
- floorLoads: array of 3 numbers representing total load per floor [floor1, floor2, floor3]
physics_constraints: Loads propagate downward: beam receives 50% of placed load, each supporting column below receives 25%. Lower floors accumulate loads from above. StressRatio = currentLoad / maxLoad. Columns maxLoad=1000kN, beams maxLoad=500kN. Structural integrity = 100 - (weightedAvgStressRatio * 100), clamped [0,100]. Total load is conserved: sum of all placed loads must equal totalLoad. Floor loads must sum to totalLoad. No NaN values in any stress calculations.
